items_missed: No "How are you today?", no formal agenda statement ("I'll gather some details, then walk you through pricing..."), and no explicit "sound good?" confirmation before diving into discovery questions
Probe skipped special considerations (narrow hallways/tight turns), exact box count, and the moving-stressors question

Pricing/differentiators barely covered: no "pricing is super simple" opener, no full what's-included list (gas, truck, taxes, insurance, bands/tools), and No Worries Damage Coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee, and the full no-hidden-fees pitch were all omitted despite quoting a detailed two-day price
Clock explanation missing the "contract opens on-site" framing and no sense-check ("does that make sense?") after walking through the hourly/prorated structure
Estimate walkthrough skipped specialty items, walk distance, equivalents (school bus, etc.), and traffic caveats
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech skipped — no consolidation tips (toys, garden tools, drawers, photos) and no "take a carload" tip

No attempt to book the date on this call (ended on "we'll review it and get back to you"); no explicit no-deposit mention, no verbal "reply with any corrections" ask, and no hours/how-to-reach-us close
Customer's name used only once ("Susan") across a 16-minute call
No insurance/damage-coverage explanation (No Worries + 60¢/lb), and no Sparefoot/Ecobox storage referral despite a storage-unit stop being part of the move
top_strength: Thorough, transparent two-day pricing breakdown (packing day + move day, materials vs. hourly rate vs. trip fee all itemized) with an honest note that he padded the estimate to leave room for packing to run long — builds trust instead of setting up a bait-and-switch on move day.
coaching_note: The core pitch mechanics (discovery, day-by-day pricing, email handoff) are solid, but every required differentiator got skipped — No Worries Damage Coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee, no-hidden-fees pitch, and the entire Save Your Ass prep speech never came up. Those are worth real dollars and reduced move-day surprises; add them as a standing checklist before the email close, and try attempting to lock the date live rather than ending on 'we'll get back to you.'
phone_presence_notes: Consistent warm, affirming language ("Perfect," "Absolutely," "good deal"), a genuine moment congratulating the customer on a new grandbaby, and enough comfort that the family put him on speakerphone to listen in — customer stayed engaged and positive throughout.
